## SVG Dashboard — Architecture Deep Dive

### Rendering Strategy: Why SVG over Canvas/WebGL

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|----------|------|------|
| **SVG** | CSS-animatable, DOM-accessible, clickable nodes, scales infinitely, text selectable, small file size | Many elements can lag >1000 nodes |
| Canvas 2D | Fast for many elements, pixel control | No DOM access, text blurry on zoom, manual hit detection |
| WebGL | 60fps at massive scale | Overkill for dashboards, steep dev cost |

**Decision**: SVG. Our dashboard has ~200 elements maximum — well within SVG's comfort zone. Every component stays clickable and styleable via CSS.

### Component Tree

```
command-control.html
├── Header bar (time, user, system health dot)
├── Bento Grid Container (CSS grid 12-col)
│   ├── [#1] Boot Sequence Panel (span 6, row 2)
│   │   ├── SVG viewBox="0 0 400 200"
│   │   ├── 4 LED bars × 10 circles each (40 total)
│   │   ├── CSS @keyframes fill-led-bar staggered 0.5s per bar
│   │   └── Status labels: "Kernel Scan", "Integrity Check", "Network Clear", "Boot OK"
│   │
│   ├── [#2] Trinity Status (span 3, row 2)
│   │   ├── 3 status cards: docker ● / mcp ● / localhost ●
│   │   ├── Live health from docker compose ps
│   │   └── Click to expand service details
│   │
│   ├── [#3] Agents Panel (span 3, row 2)
│   │   ├── AG001 Trinity — status, role, last heartbeat
│   │   ├── AG007 [vacant] — provision button
│   │   └── SVG pulse rings around active agents
│   │
│   ├── [#4] Resource Gauges (span 6, row 1)
│   │   ├── SVG arc gauges: CPU, Memory, Redis conns, HTTP req/s
│   │   ├── stroke-dasharray reveals vs total
│   │   └── Color thresholds: green <60%, amber <85%, red >85%
│   │
│   ├── [#5] Network Topology (span 6, row 3)
│   │   ├── SVG graph: nginx→app→redis, nginx→prometheus
│   │   ├── Animated dash lines (data flow)
│   │   ├── Node color = live health (green/red)
│   │   └── Click node → navigate to service
│   │
│   └── [#6] Event Log (span 12, row 2)
│       ├── Scrollable log with monospace text
│       ├── Color-coded: green=info, amber=warn, red=error
│       └── Auto-scrolls to latest, max 200 lines buffer
```

### Data Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Polling Loop (JS)                 │
│                                                     │
│  setInterval 5s ──→ docker compose ps --format json │
│                 ──→ GET /health (app)               │
│                 ──→ GET /api/v1/query?query=up      │
│                                                     │
│  setInterval 10s ─→ docker stats --no-stream        │
│                                                     │
│  setInterval 15min → Open-Meteo API (weather)       │
│                                                     │
│              ↓ Updates ↓                            │
│                                                     │
│  SVG attribute: setAttribute('fill', color)         │
│  SVG attribute: setAttribute('opacity', val)        │
│  textContent: .textContent = newValue               │
│  classList: .classList.toggle('online/offline')     │
│  Log prepend: .insertBefore(newRow, firstChild)     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### SVG Techniques Used

**1. LED Boot Bar Animation**
```svg
<circle cx="20" cy="20" r="4" class="led" style="animation-delay: 0.1s"/>
<circle cx="36" cy="20" r="4" class="led" style="animation-delay: 0.2s"/>
<!-- 10 circles per bar, each delayed 0.1s → 1s bar fill -->
```
```css
.led { fill: #1a1a2e; }
.led.boot { animation: light-up 0.3s forwards; }
@keyframes light-up { to { fill: #00e5ff; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 4px #00e5ff); } }
```

**2. Arc Gauge (CPU/Memory)**
```svg
<circle cx="60" cy="60" r="50" fill="none" 
        stroke="#1a1a28" stroke-width="8"/>
<circle cx="60" cy="60" r="50" fill="none" 
        stroke="var(--accent)" stroke-width="8"
        stroke-dasharray="314" stroke-dashoffset="94"
        stroke-linecap="round" transform="rotate(-90 60 60)"/>
```
`dashoffset = circumference × (1 - percentage/100)`

**3. Network Graph — Animated Data Flow**
```svg
<line x1="100" y1="80" x2="220" y2="80" 
      stroke="var(--accent)" stroke-width="2"
      stroke-dasharray="6 4" class="flow-line"/>
```
```css
.flow-line { animation: flow 1s linear infinite; }
@keyframes flow { to { stroke-dashoffset: -20; } }
```

**4. Agent Pulse Ring**
```svg
<circle cx="50" cy="50" r="16" fill="none" 
        stroke="var(--accent2)" stroke-width="1.5" 
        class="pulse-ring" opacity="0"/>
```
```css
.pulse-ring {
  animation: ping 2s ease-out infinite;
  transform-origin: 50px 50px;
}
@keyframes ping {
  0% { r: 12; opacity: 0.8; }
  100% { r: 30; opacity: 0; }
}
```

### Event Log — Message Format

```
[HH:MM:SS.mmm] [LEVEL] source.component: message
[04:30:13.421] [INFO] system.health: app container healthy (uptime 5,618s)
[04:30:12.108] [INFO] agent.trinity: heartbeat acknowledged
[04:30:00.000] [INFO] weather.wagga: 6.3°C, partly cloudy, wind 0.7km/h N
[04:29:45.332] [WARN] resource.cpu: 72% utilization — above threshold
[04:29:15.001] [INFO] network.nginx: 200 GET /clock.html (1.2ms)
```

### Interactions Per Panel

| Panel | Click | Result |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Boot Sequence | Replay button | Restarts LED animation |  
| Trinity docker card | Click | Opens `docker compose ps` output inline |
| Trinity localhost card | Click | Navigates to `http://localhost/` |
| AG001 Trinity agent | Click | Opens agent detail: role, permissions, config |
| AG007 vacant | Click | Opens agent provisioning form |
| nginx node (topology) | Click | Opens `http://localhost/` in new tab |
| app node (topology) | Click | Opens `http://localhost:3000/health` |
| redis node (topology) | Click | Opens redis CLI stats |
| Resource gauge | Hover | Tooltip with exact value + history sparkline |
| Event log row | Click | Expands row with full detail |

### Single File, Zero Dependencies

No npm, no frameworks, no CDN imports. Single `command-control.html` with:
- `<style>` block (~200 lines CSS)
- `<svg>` blocks embedded inline per panel
- `<script>` block (~300 lines JS) for polling + DOM updates
- Served directly by nginx on `http://localhost/command-control.html`

This is the complete architecture. Ready to build — shall I proceed with implementation?
